rules.title: Probation of 180 days or less
rules.check: probationDays <= 180 in total, including any extension or renewal of probation.
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that sets, extends or repeats the probationary period so that it exceeds 180 days in total.
rules.note: Art. 53 as amended in 2025 caps probation at 180 days in total. Probation may be split into several periods only if they are consecutive and stated in the contract.
rules.employeeMsg: Your probation is longer than the law allows. Probation is capped at 180 days in total, so the extra days are likely void.
rules.hrMsg: Probation exceeds the 180-day statutory maximum (Art. 53, as amended in 2025). The excess is likely void. Reduce it to 180 days or less.
rules.askFor: Ask for the probation period to be cut to 180 days or less.
rules.suggestedWording: The Second Party shall be subject to a probationary period of [N] days, not exceeding 180 days in total. Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha holidays, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave are not counted in the probationary period.
rules.goodMsg: Your probation of {value} days is within the 180-day legal maximum.

rules.title: Only the permitted days pause probation
rules.check: probationExcludedDays contains only eid_al_fitr, eid_al_adha, national_day, foundation_day and sick_leave.
rules.employeeMsg: Your contract pauses probation for days the law doesn't list. Only the two Eid holidays, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave can extend it.
rules.hrMsg: The probation clause excludes days that Exec. Reg. Art. 19 does not list. Exclude only Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave.
rules.askFor: Ask for the days that pause probation to be limited to the two Eid holidays, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave.
rules.suggestedWording: The following shall not be counted in the probationary period: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha holidays, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave.
rules.goodMsg: Only the days the law allows (the two Eid holidays, National Day, Foundation Day and sick leave) pause your probation.

rules.title: No compensation if the contract ends during probation
rules.check: Always applies while a probationary period is running.
rules.employeeMsg: If either side ends the contract during probation, you get no compensation and no end-of-service award.
rules.hrMsg: Ending the contract during probation triggers no compensation for either party and no end-of-service award (Art. 54).

rules.title: At least 21 days' annual leave (30 after 5 years)
rules.check: annualLeaveDays >= 21, and >= 30 once the worker has 5 consecutive years of service with the employer.
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that grants fewer than 21 days of annual leave a year (or fewer than 30 after five years of service), or otherwise reduces the annual leave in clause 8.1.
rules.employeeMsg: Your annual leave is below the legal minimum: at least 21 days a year, rising to 30 after 5 years with the same employer.
rules.hrMsg: Annual leave is below the Art. 109 minimum (21 days, or 30 after 5 consecutive years of service). The shortfall is likely void and the missing days can be claimed.
rules.askFor: Ask for at least 21 days of paid annual leave a year, rising to 30 days after 5 years of service.
rules.suggestedWording: The Second Party shall be entitled to paid annual leave of [21 or more] days a year, increasing to not less than 30 days after five consecutive years of service with the First Party.
rules.goodMsg: You get {value} days of annual leave a year. The legal minimum is 21, rising to 30 after 5 years.

rules.title: Untaken leave can't be forfeited
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that makes untaken annual leave lapse or be forfeited, or that denies cash for untaken leave when the contract ends. A clause that only says leave must be used within the year and cannot be carried forward is the weaker case.
rules.note: Refusing carry-over in advance is lawful (Art. 110); forfeiture is not, because Art. 111 requires payment for untaken leave and Art. 8 voids any waiver. Only 'no carry-over': verdict unclear, severity low. Forfeited or unpaid: verdict likely_void, severity medium.
rules.employeeMsg: Your employer can refuse to let you carry leave over, but you can't lose untaken leave or the cash for it. Unused days must be paid when you leave.
rules.hrMsg: A 'no carry-over' rule is lawful (Art. 110), but don't word it as forfeiture: Art. 111 still requires payment for untaken leave, and Art. 8 voids any waiver of it.
rules.askFor: Ask for the clause to say that any leave you haven't taken is paid in cash when the contract ends.
rules.suggestedWording: Annual leave should be taken in the year it falls due and may be carried forward only with the First Party's approval. Any accrued leave not taken when the contract ends shall be paid to the Second Party in accordance with Article 111 of the Labor Law.

rules.title: Normal hours within 8 a day and 48 a week
rules.check: dailyHours <= 8 and weeklyHours <= 48 (Muslim workers in Ramadan: 6 a day, 36 a week).
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that raises normal working hours above 8 a day or 48 a week (6 a day or 36 a week for Muslim workers in Ramadan).
rules.employeeMsg: Your normal working hours are above the legal cap of 8 hours a day or 48 a week. Hours beyond the cap count as overtime and must be paid as overtime.
rules.hrMsg: Normal working hours exceed the Art. 98 limits (8 a day and 48 a week; 6 and 36 for Muslim workers in Ramadan). Hours beyond the cap must be treated and paid as overtime.
rules.askFor: Ask for normal hours of no more than 8 a day and 48 a week, with anything beyond paid as overtime.
rules.suggestedWording: Normal working hours shall not exceed 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week, reduced to 6 hours a day or 36 hours a week for Muslim workers during Ramadan. Any additional hours shall be paid as overtime under Article 107 of the Labor Law.
rules.goodMsg: Your normal week is {value} hours, within the legal cap of 48 hours (8 a day).

rules.title: Overtime paid at the hourly wage plus 50% of basic
rules.check: overtimePremiumPct >= 50 (clause 11.2: hourly wage plus at least 50% of the basic hourly wage).
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that pays overtime at less than the hourly wage plus 50% of the basic hourly wage, or replaces overtime pay with time off in lieu without the worker's consent. A clause that requires extra hours without saying they are paid as overtime is the weaker case (verdict unclear, severity medium).
rules.note: Art. 107 as amended in 2025. Paid compensatory leave instead of overtime pay is lawful only with the worker's consent, so 'time off in lieu at the employer's discretion' fails.
rules.employeeMsg: Overtime must pay your normal hourly wage plus 50% of your basic hourly wage. Time off instead of overtime pay needs your written consent.
rules.hrMsg: The overtime terms fall below Art. 107 (amended 2025): hourly wage plus 50% of the basic hourly wage. Compensatory leave instead of pay requires the worker's written consent.
rules.askFor: Ask for overtime to be paid at your hourly wage plus 50% of your basic hourly wage, with time off in lieu only when you agree in writing.
rules.suggestedWording: Overtime hours shall be paid at the hourly wage plus 50% of the basic hourly wage. With the Second Party's written (or electronic) consent, the First Party may grant paid compensatory leave instead of overtime pay.
rules.goodMsg: Overtime pays your hourly wage plus {value}% of your basic hourly wage. The legal minimum is 50%.

rules.title: End-of-service award on the actual wage
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that calculates the end-of-service award on the basic salary only, or on any base below the last actual wage (basic plus allowances). Excluding only commissions, sales percentages and similar variable pay is allowed (Art. 86).
rules.note: Art. 2 (as amended in 2025) defines wage as the actual wage, and Art. 84 uses the last wage. Report impactParams.eosBase: basic, actual or other.
rules.employeeMsg: Likely void: your end-of-service award must be calculated on your full actual wage (basic plus allowances), not on basic salary only. Don't accept a basic-only payout.
rules.hrMsg: Likely void and unenforceable (Arts. 2, 84 and 8, and contract clause 14.5). Base the award on the last actual wage; only variable pay such as commissions may be excluded (Art. 86).
rules.askFor: Ask for the clause to be deleted, or reworded so the award is calculated on your last actual wage.
rules.suggestedWording: The end-of-service award shall be calculated on the basis of the Second Party's last actual wage, in accordance with Article 84 of the Labor Law.

rules.title: Fixed compensation for ending the contract without a valid reason
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that fixes the compensation either party pays for ending the contract without a valid reason, for example 'two months of basic wage'.
rules.note: Lawful: Art. 77 lets the contract fix the amount. Without it the default is the wages for the rest of a fixed term (15 days per year of service for an indefinite contract), with a floor of two months' wage; whether the floor is measured on actual or basic wage is open. Verdict worse_than_default. Report impactParams.compensationMonths and compensationBase (basic or actual).
rules.employeeMsg: This clause replaces your legal default (your wages for the rest of the term) with a fixed amount, which can be much less if your contract is ended early without a valid reason.
rules.hrMsg: Lawful under Art. 77, which lets the contract fix the amount. If it is measured on basic wage it may fall below the two-month floor in Art. 77; measure it on the actual wage.
rules.askFor: Ask for the compensation to be at least two months of your total wage, or for the clause to be deleted so the Art. 77 default applies.
rules.suggestedWording: If either party terminates this contract for a reason that is not valid, the other party shall be entitled to compensation equal to [N] months of the actual wage, and in any case not less than two months of the actual wage.

rules.title: Section 15 contradicts the contract type
rules.detect: A Section 15 statement about the contract's duration or type (for example 'unlimited period' or 'ends when the project ends') that contradicts the contract type, term or end date in Section 1 and clause 5.
rules.note: Under clause 14.5 an additional term that contradicts the contract is void, and under 14.8.1 the contract type can only change through Qiwa, so the Qiwa contract type most likely prevails.
rules.employeeMsg: Your contract contradicts itself on how long it lasts. The contract type recorded on Qiwa most likely wins, so keep a copy of the Qiwa record.
rules.hrMsg: Section 15 contradicts the contract type in Section 1. Under clause 14.5 the additional term is likely void, and under 14.8.1 the type can only change through Qiwa. Change the type on Qiwa or delete the term.
rules.askFor: Ask for the conflicting clause to be deleted, or for the contract type to be changed properly on Qiwa so there is one clear answer.
rules.suggestedWording: Delete the clause. If a different contract type is intended, amend the contract type on the Qiwa portal as clause 14.8.1 provides.

rules.title: Project-based ending without a defined project
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that ties the end of the contract to the completion of a project or specific work (Art. 57) without defining that work: its scope, deliverable and how completion is decided.
rules.note: Art. 57 is real: a contract for a specific work ends when that work is done. The problem is an undefined project, which leaves the end date uncertain. Verdict unclear.
rules.employeeMsg: A 'the job ends when the project ends' clause only works if the project is clearly defined. This one isn't, so you can't tell when your contract ends.
rules.hrMsg: A specific-work contract (Art. 57) needs the work defined: scope, deliverable and end criterion. As written, the end date is uncertain. Define the work, or rely on the fixed term recorded on Qiwa.
rules.askFor: Ask for the project to be defined in writing (scope and end point), or for the clause to be deleted so the fixed term applies.
rules.suggestedWording: Delete the clause, or define the work: 'This contract is for the performance of [specific work: scope and deliverable]. It ends when [objective completion criterion], as confirmed in writing by both parties.'

rules.title: Renewed fixed-term contracts become open-ended
rules.check: Saudi worker on a fixed-term contract: it becomes indefinite after 3 consecutive renewals, or once the original term plus renewals reach 4 years, whichever comes first.
rules.employeeMsg: If your fixed-term contract is renewed 3 times in a row, or reaches 4 years in total, it becomes an open-ended contract.
rules.hrMsg: Track renewals: a Saudi worker's fixed-term contract becomes indefinite after 3 consecutive renewals or 4 years in total, whichever comes first (Art. 55(2)).

rules.title: Non-renewal notice deadline
rules.check: deadline = endDate minus renewalNoticeDays. Produces a Deadline, never a scored finding.
rules.employeeMsg: To stop your contract from renewing automatically, give notice on Qiwa by {deadline}. After that date it renews for another full term.
rules.hrMsg: Non-renewal notice is due on Qiwa by {deadline}. A late notice means the contract renews for a full term (clause 5.1).

rules.title: Notice periods on an open-ended contract
rules.check: Only when contractType is indefinite. Monthly-paid worker: 30 days' written notice from the worker, 60 days from the employer; whoever skips the notice pays wages for the notice period.
rules.employeeMsg: On an open-ended contract you must give 30 days' written notice to resign, and your employer must give you 60. Whoever skips the notice pays wages for the notice period.
rules.hrMsg: Indefinite contracts need 60 days' written notice from the employer (30 from the worker), or pay in lieu of notice (Art. 75 as amended in 2025, and Art. 76).

rules.title: Transfer anywhere in the Kingdom
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that lets the employer transfer or relocate the worker to another city, branch, site or project anywhere in the Kingdom.
rules.note: Lawful and enforceable: Exec. Reg. Art. 20 treats this clause as the worker's written consent to relocation under Art. 58. Verdict worse_than_default, never likely_void.
rules.employeeMsg: Legal, but by signing you agree in advance to relocate anywhere in Saudi Arabia. If that matters to you, negotiate a limit.
rules.hrMsg: Enforceable: Exec. Reg. Art. 20 treats this clause as the worker's written consent to relocation under Art. 58. Keep it only if you need that mobility.
rules.askFor: Ask to limit transfers to your current city, or to require your agreement and relocation costs for any move that changes where you live.
rules.suggestedWording: The First Party may transfer the Second Party to another work location within [city or region]. A transfer that requires a change of residence needs the Second Party's written consent, and the First Party shall bear the relocation costs.

rules.title: Non-compete after the contract ends
rules.check: Valid only if written, specific in time, place and type of work, no longer than 2 years after the contract ends, and only where the work gives access to the employer's clients.
rules.detect: A Section 15 clause that stops the worker from working for a competitor, or competing with the employer, after the contract ends.
rules.note: Verdict compliant when every condition holds. Likely void when it lasts more than 2 years, has no limit on place or type of work, or the job gives no access to clients. Report impactParams.nonCompeteMonths when stated.
rules.employeeMsg: This non-compete is likely void. A non-compete only holds if it is specific (time, place and type of work), lasts 2 years or less, and your job gives you access to clients.
rules.hrMsg: Art. 83(1): a non-compete must be written, specific in time, place and type of work, no longer than 2 years after the contract ends, and justified by the worker's access to clients. Otherwise it is likely void.
rules.askFor: Ask for the non-compete to be deleted, or limited to 2 years or less, a named area and your specific role.
rules.suggestedWording: For [N, at most 24] months after this contract ends, the Second Party shall not work for a direct competitor of the First Party in [city or region] in a [specific role], because the Second Party's work gives access to the First Party's clients.

rules.title: Confidentiality with no limits
rules.detect: A Section 15 confidentiality clause that continues after the contract ends with no limit on time, scope or the kind of information covered.
rules.note: Keeping business secrets during employment is a normal duty (Art. 65). After the contract ends, Art. 83(2) wants the secrecy term written and specific in time, place and type of work. Verdict unclear.
rules.employeeMsg: Keeping business secrets is standard, but this clause has no end date and no limits on what counts as confidential.
rules.hrMsg: Art. 83(2) requires post-termination secrecy terms to be written and specific in time, place and type of work. Add a scope and a time limit.
rules.askFor: Ask for the clause to define what counts as confidential and how long it applies after you leave.
rules.suggestedWording: During employment and for [N] years after it ends, the Second Party shall not disclose the First Party's trade secrets, client lists or [defined categories of information] to which the Second Party had access through the work.

rules.title: Final pay deadline
rules.check: Final wages and dues within 1 week if the employer ends the contract, 2 weeks if the worker ends it.
rules.employeeMsg: When your job ends, your final pay and dues are due within 1 week, or 2 weeks if you resign.
rules.hrMsg: Settle final wages and dues within 1 week when the employer ends the contract, or 2 weeks when the worker does (Art. 88).

rules.title: Housing and transport allowances vs market norm
rules.check: Housing about 25% of basic (within 5 points) and transport about 10% of basic (within 3 points). Below: worse_than_default, low. At: compliant. Above: better_than_law. Market convention, not law.
rules.employeeMsg: Your housing and transport allowances are {position} the usual market split (housing about 25% of basic salary, transport about 10%). This is a market convention, not a legal requirement.
rules.hrMsg: The allowance split is {position} the market convention (housing about 25% of basic, transport about 10%). Not a legal requirement.
rules.askFor: Ask whether housing can be raised to about 25% of your basic salary and transport to about 10%.
rules.suggestedWording: Housing allowance: [25]% of the basic wage. Transportation allowance: [10]% of the basic wage.
rules.goodMsg: Your housing and transport allowances are {position} the usual market split (25% and 10% of basic salary).
